subject: Post-call: grounding risk mitigation, recommended rerankers & benchmarks (Lyra Health)
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Post-call: grounding risk mitigation, recommended rerankers & benchmarks (Lyra Health)

Hi Alyssa —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we keep momentum on the evaluation: you, you mentioned your biggest concerns are (1) hallucination risk on sensitive clinical guidance, (2) preserving low-latency interactive responses for care coordinators, and (3) being able to demonstrate measurable grounding improvements to your security/compliance team.

Where we landed in the call:
- Recommended baseline model: Redwood-1.7b-quant (good tradeoff for latency/cost) for initial pilots, with a plan to test Redwood-7b/Redwood-13b if recall/answer quality falls short.
- Retrieval: hybrid vector store (semantic + exact-match) with a 10k token chunking policy for your KB. We suggested a top-K retrieval of 12 and a diversity penalty on near-duplicate text.
- Reranker: two options — a light cross-encoder (rerank-lite) for sub-second ranking on high-priority queries, and a heavier cross-encoder (rerank-xl) for nightly batch evaluation where latency is not critical.
- Grounding metrics to track: hallucination rate (factually incorrect assertions per 100 responses), source-citation coverage (percent of responses with at least one direct citation), and precision@1 for top answer correctness on the 200-case clinical prompt set we discussed.

Attached are two artifacts I promised: a CSV with the seed benchmark prompts + expected answers (lyra_grounding_benchmarks.csv) and a short note comparing the two reranker options (reranker_comparison_notes.pdf).

Immediate next steps (action owners in-line):
1) We’ll provision a sandbox project and load a 5k-doc slice of your KB for a smoke test — (Redwood) — ETA: Tue 8/24.
2) Lyra to confirm a preferred 200-case prompt subset for the clinical regression tests and flag any internal redlines — (Lyra) — ETA: Wed 8/25.
3) Redwood to deliver a one-page SLA risk mitigation plan that describes fallback policies (model variant fallbacks, deterministic citation-first mode), labeling guidelines for false positives in evals, and how we’ll instrument audit logs — (Kim) — ETA: Thu 8/26.

Questions we have for you to unblock the pilot setup:
- Can you grant sandbox read access to integrations@lyrahealth.com for the sample KB?
- Is 99 ms 95th percentile token latency acceptable for interactive workflows, or do we need to target a tighter SLO?

I’ll follow up with the sandbox invite and the HubSpot deal update.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Hi Kim —

Really helpful summary, thanks. A couple quick clarifications before we hand the prompt set to the clinical review team:

1) Reranker latency: for the interactive coordinator UI we need per-query end-to-end (retrieve + rerank + generate) to be under 500ms P95. If rerank-lite is inline and pushes us past 500ms, are there options to do a hybrid (retrieve + model-scoring lightweight filter, then rerank in the background for audits)?

2) Fallback mode: can you explain in one sentence what "deterministic citation-first mode" does and whether it can be toggled per route? We may want the care-coordinator route to be conservative (citation-first) while chat-style routing is more permissive.

3) Access: integrations@lyrahealth.com can take a read-only token for the 5k-doc slice; I’ll ask our infra team to provision that this afternoon.

We’ll push a curated 200-case set to the folder link you shared by EOD Tuesday.

Thanks — Alyssa
VP Product
Lyra Health
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Post-call: grounding risk mitigation, recommended rerankers & benchmarks (Lyra Health)

Hi Alyssa —

Quick technical notes to address your two questions:

- Reranker latency and hybrid approach:
  * rerank-lite is a distilled cross-encoder tuned for score separation on short clinical queries; on a T4-like instance we typically see ~120-180ms per rerank for a 12-candidate set. With retrieve (vector search ~50ms) + rerank-lite (~150ms) + generate baseline (~150ms), P95 can be ~350-450ms depending on prompt length and tokenization. That keeps you under 500ms P95 in many of our trials.
  * Hybrid option: yes — implement a two-stage flow: (1) lightweight lexical/fast model score to filter 30->12 candidates (<=60ms), (2) rerank-lite for final ordering. The background auditing rerank-xl can be applied asynchronously to flagged queries.

- Deterministic citation-first mode (one-liner): force the generation policy to only surface responses when there is at least one retrieved passage with a similarity score above a configurable threshold; otherwise return a safe canned response and an explicit "no confident grounding" flag. This mode is toggled per route — we can expose it as a route-level boolean in the config.

I attached a short comparison PDF that includes microbenchmarks (latency vs. accuracy) for rerank-lite vs. rerank-xl; main takeaway: rerank-lite reduces hallucination by ~22% vs retrieval-only while staying within interactive SLOs for typical corpora.

Happy to walk through numbers live if helpful.

— Karthik
Principal Applied ML Engineer
Redwood Inference
